title: Prefetch fidelity handoff and snapshot protocol - PRD (draft)
summary: Draft PRD describing a protocol and SDK ergonomics for progressive response delivery: TTL-tagged partial snapshots, snapshot handshake for resumable sessions, prefetch fidelity profiles that are backpressure-aware, and fractional/commit semantics for tool-calls and structured outputs. Goal is to improve perceived latency and reduce wasted token cost on long-running tool compositions while preserving deterministic resume and observability.
goals: Define a lightweight snapshot-handshake protocol so clients can resume partial streams deterministically
Introduce prefetch fidelity profiles (fast/medium/faithful) that the runtime and SDK negotiate to trade cost vs. fidelity
Surface fractional commit semantics for tool-calls (tentative/commit/cancel) so clients and servers can reason about side effects
Provide SDK ergonomics patterns (Snapshot API + Delta subscription + Hedged prefetch) that are easy to adopt for web and mobile clients
Ensure compatibility with existing streaming frames and tool-call contracts; offer a migration path
non_goals: We are not redesigning existing full-session persistence or long-term evaluation tooling in this PRD. This does not define a new billing model; cost telemetry will be used to inform future pricing changes.
success_metrics: Median time-to-first-meaningful-chunk decrease by 20% for conversational workloads with external tool calls
Token spend reduction of 10% for multi-step tool scaffolding through prefetch avoidance
Resume success rate >= 99.5% for interrupted sessions using snapshot handshake within the first 3 months of rollout
Adoption: 25% of hosted-api customers with streaming enabled adopt the Snapshot API within 6 months
user_stories: As a mobile developer, I want partial results quickly and then higher-fidelity replacements later, so my app shows instant progress without overfetching
As a backend developer orchestrating tool-chains, I want a clear commit signal for tool side-effects so retries and rollbacks are safe
As an SRE, I want resumeable streams to reduce error surface from flaky networks and to simplify incident mitigation
As a product manager, I want to configure fidelity profiles for different traffic classes (free vs paid) without changing client code
technical_approach: Streaming frames will include an optional 'snapshot_id' and 'ttl_ms' header on partial frames to indicate a persisted snapshot that clients can reference for resume
Runtime will maintain ephemeral snapshot stores keyed by snapshot_id with configurable TTLs; snapshots are lightweight deltas (KV of recent prefixes + tool-call guards) rather than full model state
Prefetch fidelity profiles: client sends 'prefetch_hint' (fast|balanced|faithful) at request start. Runtime uses profile to decide speculative token expansion and early tool invocation policies

Tool-call contract extended to support 'tentative' mode: tentative tool calls return a provisional result that is not idempotent-guarded until a 'commit' frame is sent by the client or server policy infers commit
SDKs provide SnapshotClient with: createSnapshot(), resumeFrom(snapshot_id), subscribeDeltas(snapshot_id), and hedgedPrefetch(prefetch_hint, budget_ms) APIs
Observability: every snapshot and commit will emit events with correlating ids (snapshot_id, request_id, tool_call_id) to existing tracing; TTL expirations are logged as timeline events
sdk_ergonomics_notes: SDK focus is low-friction onboarding: default client instantiation should work without snapshots. Snapshot APIs are opt-in. Web SDK will expose a StreamingSnapshot class with an async iterator that yields 'partial' and 'replace' events. Mobile SDKs get a small helper that wires UI placeholders to partial snapshots and swaps in replacements when committed. Examples below show intended ergonomics and minimal error handling patterns.
streaming_frame_format_examples:
Example frame header (pseudo):
- frame_type: 'partial' | 'replace' | 'commit' | 'snapshot' | 'error'
- request_id: string
- snapshot_id: optional string
- ttl_ms: optional int (applies to snapshot frames)
- prefetch_hint: optional 'fast'|'balanced'|'faithful' (sent only on initial frame)

Note: 'replace' frames reference an earlier partial via snapshot_id and carry a stable 'sequence' to allow clients to reconcile out-of-order deliveries.
tool_call_handshake:
Tool-call modes: 'direct' (current behavior), 'tentative' (side-effect guarded), 'transactional' (server-coordinated).
- Tentative flow: client requests tool-call in tentative mode -> runtime forwards tentative request to tool adapter with limited-side-effect flag -> adapter returns provisional response with tool_call_id -> client later sends commit frame referencing tool_call_id (or runtime auto-commits on success heuristics).
- Server must support idempotency tokens for tentative calls and a soft-lock to prevent duplicate final commits.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (experiment): implement snapshot TTL store behind feature flag; internal users try mobile preview apps; measure resume and TTL cost impact
Phase 1 (beta): expose Snapshot API in JS/TS SDK, opt-in for customers; enable tentative tool-calls as an experimental toggle
Phase 2 (wider rollout): enable default prefetch_hint='balanced' for new streaming routes; add server-side heuristics to auto-commit low-risk tentative calls
Phase 3 (GA): document semantics, add console toggles (per-route fidelity profiles), promote SDKs and migration guides
migration_notes: Existing streaming clients will continue to work. To adopt snapshots, clients add SnapshotClient.resumeFrom(snapshot_id) and start listening for 'replace' frames. For tool-call commit semantics, customers must update tool adapters to respect tentative mode. We'll provide shims in the SDK to polyfill tentative semantics for adapters that don't support it.
observability_and_cost_considerations: Snapshots increase short-term storage and tracing events; limit default TTL to 30s for the fast profile and 5 minutes for faithful profile. Prefetch heuristics should be gated by per-route budgets and observed token-cost signals. Instrument: snapshot_write_count, snapshot_resume_latency, tentative_tool_invocations, commit_latency, speculative_token_waste_ratio.
open_questions: What should the default TTL be for the balanced profile? 30s or 60s?
Should tentative tool-calls be enabled for all adapters or only adapters that declare idempotency capability?
How to represent partial structured outputs in billing/allocations (do we bill speculative tokens?)
Server-side auto-commit heuristics: which signals (tool success probability, adapter idempotency, user action) qualify?
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: speculative prefetch increases token spend. Mitigation: per-route speculative budget, telemetry alarms, and a kill-switch in Console. Risk: complexity for adapter authors to support tentative mode. Mitigation: provide SDK shims and a reference adapter pattern with tests.
next_steps: (1) spike: implement minimal snapshot store + header parsing in runtime (2 weeks). (2) prototype SnapshotClient in JS SDK and mobile pseudo-API (3 weeks). (3) internal playtest with Solutions Eng and a customer sandbox (2 weeks).
appendices: Notes to reviewers: include sample tracing spans in the implementation PR and compare token metrics from the experiment against baseline. Attach screenshots of mobile placeholder UX when replacing partials in the beta demo (tracked in linked artifacts).
